title: Quantification of Digestive Exophagy in Cell Culture
author: Funes, Maxfield, et al.

steps.title: Set up sterile workstation
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile cell culture hood or ductless ventilation hood, sanitize with 70% ethanol, UV‑irradiate for 20 min, and gather all required tools (scissors, curved tip forceps, fine tip forceps, micro‑spatula, fine tip tweezers, scalpel). Autoclave tools, submerge them in 70% ethanol with paper wipes, and bring them into the hood. Spray a Styrofoam box and ice packs with 70% ethanol, place ice packs inside the box, and bring the box into the hood. Place three 50 mL Falcon tubes filled with CMF‑PBS and a 10 cm sterile Petri dish on the ice packs, fill the dish with cold CMF‑PBS and keep refrigerated. Place a second sterile Petri dish under the stereotaxic microscope for brain extraction.

steps.title: Prepare neonatal mouse heads
steps.instruction: Select mouse neonates aged 2–3 days, transport them in an approved container, sterilize the container exterior with 70% ethanol, and place the container inside the sterile workstation.

steps.title: Euthanize pup and collect head
steps.instruction: Place a pup on the Petri dish, wipe the top of its head with a 70% ethanol‑soaked paper wipe, decapitate with sterilized scissors, dispose of the carcass in a biohazard bag, and keep the head on ice.

steps.title: Extract brain from head
steps.instruction: Using sterilized tweezers, anchor the head by the nose. With a scalpel, incise the skin from front to back, move the skin aside, then cut through the skull without puncturing the brain. Slide a sterilized spatula sideways under the brain, lift it gently, and place the extracted brain in the Petri dish filled with cold CMF‑PBS.

steps.title: Process all pup brains
steps.instruction: Repeat euthanasia and brain extraction for each pup, changing the scalpel after processing 3–4 brains. Pause before meninges removal.

steps.title: Remove meninges
steps.instruction: Wipe a fresh Petri dish with 70% ethanol, add cold CMF‑PBS to the midway mark, cut the tip off a plastic transfer pipette, transfer each brain to a fresh dish with additional CMF‑PBS, hold the brain by the olfactory bulb or cerebellum with dull forceps, and carefully peel off the meninges from the cortical surface and ventral regions using sharp forceps.

steps.title: Isolate cortical tissue
steps.instruction: Cut away right and left cortical areas with sharp tweezers, transfer them with the plastic pipette into a 50 mL conical tube containing 2 mL cold CMF‑PBS, and discard remaining brain tissue into a biohazard bag. Keep cortices on ice.

steps.title: Settle cortices
steps.instruction: Allow cortices to settle to the bottom of the tube; do not place cortices from more than 4–5 mice in a single tube.

steps.title: Warm media and enzymes
steps.instruction: Warm complete DMEM medium, trypsin, and DNAse aliquots to 37 °C in a water bath (do not exceed 30 min in the bath).

steps.title: Wash and mince cortices
steps.instruction: Aspirate the top CMF‑PBS layer and wash cortices 3 × with 3 mL fresh CMF‑PBS (avoid aspirating tissue). Add 5 mL fresh CMF‑PBS, mince with a scalpel, and triturate about 30 times. Let the minced tissue settle.

steps.title: Trypsinize cortices
steps.instruction: Remove the PBS layer, add 1 mL warm trypsin solution containing trypsin, DNAse, and MgSO₄ using a 5 mL serological pipette, pipette up/down 3 times, and incubate 5 min at 37 °C while swirling gently once per minute.

steps.title: Homogenize post‑trypsin tissue
steps.instruction: Return tubes to the workstation, attach a rubber bulb to a glass pipette, transfer the gelatinous tissue into a 15 mL conical tube containing 2 mL warm DNAse buffer, pipette up/down until fully homogenized, then spin at 400 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Collect and plate mixed cell culture
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, note the two‑layer pellet (light top layer = cells, reddish bottom = debris). Using a fresh glass pipette with rubber bulb, collect only the light‑colored top layer and transfer to a 50 mL tube with 10 mL DMEM. Resuspend gently, add another 10 mL DMEM, and transfer the 20 mL suspension into a 75 cm² vented T75 flask. Label the flask with date, number of brains, pup age, etc. Place flasks in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: First medium change (day 2)
steps.instruction: Collect the spent medium from each flask into a 50 mL tube, add 10 mL fresh medium to the flask, spin the collected medium at 500 × g for 4 min, filter through a 0.4 µm filter, re‑warm the filtrate to 37 °C, and wash each flask gently with 10 mL warm DMEM three times (discard each wash). Finally, add 15 mL filtered medium plus 10 mL fresh medium to each flask and return to the incubator.

steps.title: Culture maturation (10–14 days)
steps.instruction: Maintain the flasks for 10–14 days. Verify under a microscope that an astrocytic layer (flat, elongated, dark cells) underlies the microglial cells (small bright dots).

steps.title: Harvest microglia from flasks
steps.instruction: Aspirate old medium and add 20 mL warm phenol‑red‑free DMEM to each flask. Incubate 1 h at 37 °C. Prepare a heater blower and orbital shaker, spray surfaces with 70% ethanol, wrap flask caps tightly with parafilm, place flasks on the shaker set to 37 °C, and shake at 1–3 Hz for 2 h. Transfer the medium containing lifted microglia into 15 mL tubes (10 mL per tube). Add 20 mL fresh medium to each empty flask and rinse gently to release remaining cells. Centrifuge all tubes at 500 × g for 4 min, aspirate supernatant, resuspend each pellet in 1 mL warm phenol‑red‑free DMEM, count cells, prepare a working stock as needed, and seed microglia for downstream assays.

steps.title: Label Aβ42 with Alexa647
steps.instruction: Solubilize 1 mg monomeric Aβ42 in 1000 µL cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3. Prepare a 10 mg/mL Alexa 647‑NHS stock in dry DMSO (1 mg in 100 µL). Add the Alexa 647 stock to the peptide solution, and incubate 1 h at 4 °C with slow rotation.

steps.title: Dialyze Alexa647‑Aβ42
steps.instruction: Fill a sterile beaker with 4 L cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3 and add a magnetic stir bar. Load the reaction into a 3.5 kDa dialysis cassette, attach to a sterile foam holder, and stir for 3 h at 4 °C. Replace the buffer and dialyze 12 h, then perform a third 3 h dialysis the next morning. Keep the beaker covered with foil throughout.

steps.title: Aliquot Alexa647‑labeled peptide
steps.instruction: Extract the dialyzed peptide from the cassette with a sterile 1 mL syringe, split into 50 µL aliquots, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine Alexa647 incorporation
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance of the aliquots to calculate the Alexa 647:Aβ42 molar ratio (batch used: 1:1.12, 221 µM Aβ42, 249 µM Alexa 647).

steps.title: Prepare fAβ42 aggregation mixture
steps.instruction: Solubilize 1 mg Aβ42 in 123 µL cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3 (221 µM). Solubilize 0.2 mg Aβ42‑biotin in 114 µL same buffer. Add 49.5 µL Alexa 647‑Aβ42, 114 µL biotin‑Aβ42, and the 123 µL unlabeled Aβ42 into a 1.5 mL tube, bring volume to 1272 µL with 1× PBS. Add 40 µL 1 N HCl, measure pH with indicator strips, and adjust with additional 1 N HCl to ~pH 5 (do not use NaOH). Incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C with constant rotation. Centrifuge at 21 000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS, spin again, and repeat centrifugation steps until the supernatant is clear.

steps.title: Streptavidin‑label aggregates
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 mM streptavidin stock (54.3 mg in 1 mL 1× PBS). Remove supernatant from the fAβ42‑biotin‑Alexa647 pellet, add the entire streptavidin solution, resuspend, and incubate 1 h at 37 °C with rotation. Spin at 21 000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, and repeat washing 3 times. Finally, resuspend the pellet in 1.5 mL 1× PBS (final 170 µM fAβ42) and store at 4 °C (use within 1–2 weeks) or at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label Aβ42 with fluorescein
steps.instruction: Solubilize 1 mg monomeric Aβ42 in 1000 µL cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3. Prepare a 50 mg/mL fluorescein‑NHS stock in dry DMSO (1 g in 20 mL). Add 8.4 µL fluorescein‑NHS stock to the peptide solution, and incubate 1 h at 4 °C with slow rotation.

steps.title: Dialyze fluorescein‑Aβ42
steps.instruction: Dialyze the reaction as described for Alexa647‑Aβ42 (3 × 3 h/12 h/3 h dialysis against cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3).

steps.title: Aliquot fluorescein‑labeled peptide
steps.instruction: Extract the dialyzed peptide, split into 50 µL aliquots, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine fluorescein incorporation
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance to calculate the fluorescein:Aβ42 ratio (batch used: 1:0.93, 221 µM Aβ42, 206 µM fluorescein).

steps.title: Prepare fluorescein‑biotin fAβ42 aggregation
steps.instruction: Solubilize 1 mg Aβ42 in 123 µL cold 50 mM sodium tetraborate pH 9.3, and 0.2 mg Aβ42‑biotin in 114 µL same buffer. Combine fluorescein‑Aβ42 (60 µL), biotin‑Aβ42 (114 µL), and unlabeled Aβ42 (122 µL) in a 1.5 mL tube, bring volume to 1272 µL with 1× PBS, add 40 µL 1 N HCl, adjust pH to ~5 with additional 1 N HCl, incubate 12–18 h at 37 °C with rotation, centrifuge 21 000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS, spin again, and repeat until supernatant is clear.

steps.title: Sonicate and triturate aggregates
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in 2 mL 1× PBS, sonicate in a water‑bath sonicator for 10 min. Split the volume into two 1 mL tubes, triturate each by loading/unloading 20 times through a 0.5 mL insulin syringe with a 28‑gauge needle, repeat the sonication‑trituration cycle once more, then combine the two aliquots (final 2 mL, 127 µM fAβ42). Store at 4 °C; before use, spin down, discard supernatant, and re‑sonicate/triturate.

description: To digest objects that are too large to be phagocytosed—such as large lipoprotein aggregates similar to those seen in atherosclerotic plaques,2,3 Alzheimer’s disease (AD) amyloid-beta (Aβ) deposits,1 or dead adipocytes4—phagocytic cells create tightly sealed extracellular regions on the target, into which protons and lysosomal contents are secreted. These compartments, which are called lysosomal synapses, are able to degrade extracellular aggregates and some large apoptotic cells.4 This process has been called digestive exophagy, and it is very similar to the well-known degradative mechanisms used by osteoclasts during bone resorption.5 In the AD brain, microglia surround and engage Aβ plaques in an attempt to contain or digest6,7,8,9 their diffuse outer layers, which have been described as sources of neurotoxic oligomeric Aβ species.10,11,12 Digestive exophagy by microglia might help contain Aβ pathology. However, under some circumstances, previously endocytosed lysosomal contents, including fibrillar (f) Aβ, can be released into lysosomal synapses and contribute to plaque growth and/or spread.1 Given the novelty and pathological relevance of this mechanism, we prepared two standardized protocols to measure digestive exophagy of fAβ42 model aggregates by primary murine microglial cells. Our methodology consists of two sections: measuring lysosomal exocytosis toward lysosomal synapses established on fAβ42 aggregates, and measuring the extracellular degradation of surface-immobilized fAβ42 fibrils. The combination of these two readouts provides a direct assessment of digestive exophagy. We also developed protocols to image and quantify the pH of lysosomal synapses created by microglial cells on fAβ42 model aggregates. For these assays we typically use fluorescein or our new pH sensor ApHID13 as pH-sensitive reporters.
